title: The Sunni telling
hookLine: Sunni Muslims hold that the community chose Abu Bakr by consultation and pledge

lines: A LEADER FROM US, AND FROM YOU.
cards: Under the roof of the saqifah the voices are rising. A leader from us and a leader from you, the Ansar have said. Abu Bakr has put forward two other men, Umar and Abu Ubaydah: pledge to whichever of them you choose.
Then Umar, by his own account in Sahih al-Bukhari, turns to Abu Bakr and says: stretch out your hand. Abu Bakr does. Umar places his hand in it and pledges, and others follow.
This is how Sunni Muslims tell what happened next. Today's word: khalifah.

teach.b: Khalifah is usually rendered successor or deputy, one who comes after and stands in for another.
The Qur'an uses the word in its second surah, when God tells the angels, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth."
Abu Bakr came to be called the khalifah of the Messenger of God, his successor in leading the community, though not in prophecy; revelation had ended with the Prophet. So how was he chosen?
Sunni Muslims hold that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, did not formally name a successor, and that the community chose.
They point to the pledge, the bay'ah, given hand in hand at the saqifah, and to a second, wider pledge, which Bukhari reports was taken from the people in the mosque the following day.
And to Abu Bakr's standing: when the Prophet was too ill to lead the prayer, Bukhari reports he told the people to let Abu Bakr lead it.
Sunni scholars also look to a Qur'anic description of the believers as those "whose affairs are a matter of counsel."
Consultation, shura, and pledge became, in this telling, the way the community chose. The telling is honest about the strain.
Umar himself, later, as leader of the believers, says in Bukhari that the pledge to Abu Bakr was made in haste, and that God protected the community from its harm.

He warns that no one should take a pledge without the counsel of the believers. For Sunni Muslims, then, Abu Bakr is the first of the caliphs, chosen by people who knew him. Tomorrow, the Shia telling, in its own words.

how: Sunni Muslims honor Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali as the rightly guided caliphs, and Sunni scholars discuss consultation (shura) and the pledge (bay'ah) when they write about leadership.

games.q: you're at the saqifah. Abu Bakr has put forward Umar and Abu Ubaydah and said: pledge to either. what does Umar do?
o: accepts and asks for pledges to himself.
says stretch out your hand, and pledges to Abu Bakr.
walks out to fetch the family.
games.why: by his own account in Bukhari, Umar took Abu Bakr's hand and pledged, and others followed.

practice: Bring to mind a community you belong to: a mosque, a church, a school board, a club, a family business. Ask yourself how someone comes to lead there, who gets asked and who gets heard, and notice what you don't know.
If you pray, you can pray for wisdom for whoever leads it.

wordCard.voice: Khalifah. A successor, one who stands in for another. Abu Bakr was called the khalifah of the Messenger of God, chosen, in the Sunni telling, by counsel and pledge. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a successor, one who stands in for another; in English, caliph.

carryVoice: Your line: chosen by pledge. In this telling, counsel and a hand held out. That's day eight hundred sixty-four.
